newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ housing confidence rises in April qtr -ASB Bank.
newsitem.headline: NZ housing confidence rises in April qtr -ASB Bank.

text.p: ASB Bank said on Wednesday its April Quarterly Housing Report showed a net 44 percent of respondents throughout the country expect house prices to rise over the next 12 months, up from 36 percent in the previous quarter.

Christchurch held its lead with a net 65 percent of respondents expecting prices to rise, well above 43 percent and 49 percent respectively in Auckland and Wellington. Comparable figures for the February quarter were 57 percent, 33 percent and 35 percent respectively.
ASB economist Rozanna Wozniak said that despite becoming the weakest of the regions measured in the survey, the number of optimists in Auckland continued to outweigh pessimists.
A net 37 percent of Christchurch residents said it was a good time to buy a house, compared with 29 percent in Wellington and 17 percent in Auckland.
Wozniak said confidence in the residential property market in Otago and Southland was nearly double that of the rest of New Zealand.
In the three months to April a net 67 percent of respondents in the Otago and Southland area believed it was a good time to buy a house, compared with a net 37 percent over the whole country.
In the previous quarter to February, confidence in Otago and Southland was a net 36 percent.
"This survey was conducted prior to the recent round of interest rate cuts, so in light of those cuts, confidence should remain strong over the months ahead," Wozniak said.
"Although the inflation outlook suggests there is no need for a tightening of monetary conditions until late this year, perhaps even early 1998, the currency has already shown signs of vulnerability.

"If the currency starts to weaken, upward pressure on interest rates is expected to return, particularly on the floating and short term fixed rates where recent reductions have been the largest," Wozniak said.
